open_questions: Generals tier map (choice 1 in research/registry-notes/games-r3.md). Keep the current map, or move the tech building to t2? Now: basic production t1; a General's Promotion alone t2 (Paladin, Stealth Fighter and Marauder at 1-star, Pathfinder at 3-star); the one tech building per side (Strategy Center, Propaganda Center, Palace), alone or with a promotion, t3. Facts from the 1.04 files: the tech building is one step past a factory and also opens the superweapon; every player starts at rank 1 with one point to spend, so a 1-star unit can come in the first minute; of the wiki pages read, only the Overlord, Hacker and Super hacker infoboxes give a tier (3), and the Marauder's (2). Two of choice 1's t3 examples are wrong: the Avenger needs only the War Factory and the Saboteur only the Barracks with an Arms Dealer standing, so both are t1 under either map. Choice 2 is short by one: besides the Air Force General's Stealth Fighter (t2 to t1), the Stealth General's Hijacker needs only the Barracks (t3 to t1); both are recorded under the main faction, so the bands stay and tier.basis names the exception. Options: A keep the map; B tech building alone t2, tech building plus a promotion t3, promotion alone t2 (t3 would then hold only the Nuke Cannon, SCUD Launcher and Hijacker). Recommendation: A. The tech building is each side's top tech (it opens the superweapons), which fits t3's 'top-level tech'; the wiki's own labels agree; B leaves t3 almost empty. No Generals unit is coded yet, so either choice recodes nothing.

Should Generals' laser weapons count as energy damage, as the Tempest Rising note makes every laser? In the 1.04 data the Laser Tank's gun carries ARMOR_PIERCING and the Avenger's anti-air lasers SMALL_ARMS, so armament[].damage step 4 makes them armour-piercing and kinetic, and the laser family's rule (energy or fire only) is broken and recorded in atypical. Options: A follow the damage map (the notes as written: no laser exception); B add a step-3 exception that records every Generals laser weapon as energy. Recommendation: A. The mapped types keep the game's counterplay: the Avenger's lasers are built to down light aircraft, which kinetic is strong against and energy is not, and armour-piercing and energy read the same against tanks. It affects the Avenger, a candidate of this batch, and the Laser Tank. The Angry Mob's guns and rocks, whose MOLOTOV_COCKTAIL name would make them fire, get a step-3 exception to kinetic either way, because that name says they burn and they do not.

Do the base-game manual's Purpose entries count for the Zero Hour generals' versions of a unit (Uncertain item 'Purpose lines and the generals' in research/registry-notes/games-r3.md)? Official text counts for a unit recorded once for several sides only when every side's version carries it, and the 2003 manual predates the nine generals. Options: A yes: a version keeps the main unit's in-game name and is the unit the manual describes, so its Purpose entry counts for every version (the notes as written); B no: roles step 1 would then skip the Purpose entry of nearly every base-game unit, since most are also fielded by a general. Recommendation: A, because B would throw away the game's main role text for almost every unit. A general's unit of its own (its own in-game name, such as the Laser Tank or the Toxin Rebel) has no Purpose entry either way and reads its build tooltip.

registry_edits.reason: Confirmed wrong (skeptic verdict on the sight_reference finding). The Ranger's 100 and 400 are its VisionRange and ShroudClearingRange in the 1.04 files, and the engine clears the fog only out to ShroudClearingRange; VisionRange is the targeting range and, for detectors with no detection range of their own, the detection radius. A one-figure infobox is usually the fog figure (the Angry Mob's members are 150 and 150), so comparing it with 100 mixes two scales; the skeptic's caveat (the Biohazard Technician page lists only its vision figure) is why the text sends one-figure units to the Object file.
registry_edits.value: Ranger: sight 100-400 in the wiki infobox, which are the VisionRange (100) and ShroudClearingRange (400) of its object in the unedited 1.04 files. The engine clears the fog of war out to ShroudClearingRange; VisionRange clears no fog (it is how far the unit targets and, for a detector with no detection range of its own, how far it reveals stealthed units). So use 400, and the second figure of every unit that lists two. Where the infobox lists one figure, read ShroudClearingRange in the unit's 1.04 Object file; an object without one clears the fog to its VisionRange

value.title: Object.cpp, Command & Conquer: Generals - Zero Hour source code, Electronic Arts on GitHub
value.note: A new object whose ShroudClearingRange is unset takes its VisionRange instead. The look routine lifts the fog of war for the owner and its allies out to the shroud-clearing figure; the vision figure is how far the object counts as a target or a threat, not a fog figure. Riders in transports and tunnels do not look. Other files of the same release: Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp (a detector with no DetectionRange of its own detects out to its VisionRange); Source/Common/INI/INI.cpp with Include/Common/GameCommon.h (a Speed in the INI files is a distance per second, turned into a step per logic frame at 30 frames a second); Source/GameLogic/Object/Locomotor.cpp (a walking soldier speeds up to its Speed, slowing only to turn or stop, and moves at SpeedDamaged once ActiveBody.cpp finds its health at or below GameData.ini's UnitReallyDamagedThreshold, 0.35); Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/PhysicsUpdate.cpp (no forward friction acts while a unit drives itself, so the listed Speed is its real top speed).

open_questions: Tempest Rising: does 'control' of a place name the disabler role? The build tooltips call the Peacekeeper an "air control" helicopter and the Physicist a "zone control" specialist. The roles entry in docs/vocabularies.md lets control name disabler and makes an exception only for mind control and a control point. A (what the note now says): control of a place (air control, zone control) names no role, like a control point; both units take their roles from their other words and the later steps (the Physicist still gets area denial from its line's deny areas). B: read the word list literally: both lines name disabler, which step 1 keeps only if the unit's stock parts meet disabler's requires (stun, root, silence or slow traits, cryo or emp damage, or a control pattern). C: A now, and add control of a place to the word list's no-role words at the next rule round (a change to the approved word lists 1.1.0). Recommendation: A for batch R3, then C, because these words mean holding the sky or the ground, not stopping enemies from acting, which is disabler's job. The Sniper's "combat control" names disabler under every option.

open_questions: Iron Harvest: should 'mech hunter', 'mech destroyer' and 'anti-mech' count as anti-armour words? KING Art's newest type labels call the Lowca and Wotan Mech Hunters and the Knox a Mech destroyer (DevBlog #43, https://kingart-games.com/article/119), and its game page calls the field cannons anti-mech cannons. In this game the armoured fighting machines are mechs, not tanks, so the labels mean what tank hunter and anti-tank mean elsewhere. But the roles word list names a role only through a label or alias in any word form, and anti-armour's aliases are anti-tank, anti-vehicle, anti-armor, tank hunter and tank destroyer. As written, roles step 1 gives these units nothing; the R3 notes tell coders to add an uncertain entry and report it as a rule problem. Options: (A) keep the rule, and these units take their role at a later step; (B) in the rule-fix round after R4, add 'mech hunter', 'mech destroyer' and 'anti-mech' to anti-armour's aliases and recode the units whose step 1 changes; (C) in that round, let a registry note name a game's own word for its armoured units, so that word stands in for tank or vehicle inside any alias. Recommendation: B. It is the narrowest fix, it follows the makers' own words, and the uncertain entries the R3 coders add make the recoding easy to find. C only pays off if a later game shows the same gap.
